body: The development of unofficial Grand Theft Auto VI PC ports continues. Just days after the first projects managed to render interactive gameplay, developer D Everett Hinton has shared a nearly four-minute video claiming to show the game running with several PC-specific graphics features.

items.title: AI enthusiast deletes Linux for a 24KB pure assembly OS that boots in 74 milliseconds
items.summary: An intrepid developer has deleted their Linux OS and coded a tiny assembly-language bare-metal bootable alternative to run LLMs. As well as drastically cutting resource use, it seems to work far faster.
body: Is your OS getting in the way of your computing? Rebalance your resource use.

The compact size of this Multiboot OS binary (asm-llm-os.elf) is remarkable. Weighing in at just 24KB (24,252 bytes), it makes modern operating systems seem gargantuan. However, one must remember that the legendary Commodore 64 worked off a smaller 20KB ROM, which included not only the kernel but also a BASIC interpreter and a character generator.

Fateev says that his Multiboot OS with modern SMP support was written from scratch without Linux, Windows, C, Rust, or libc. Users interact with the new OS via its support for 80x25 character color VGA displays, PS/2 keyboards, and serial communications. Such is the purposeful efficiency of this hand-written NASM assembly language project that it can boot in 74-94 milliseconds directly to its multi-turn chat interface. You're ready to chat with your LLM in the blink of an eye.

While the OS and its carefully honed UI use only a tiny portion of the computer's resources, the OS loads Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, which weighs in at 649MB. That's something of a lightweight LLM, as many of you will be aware, but it is roughly 28,000 times bigger than the OS that references it. That's good, as you bought your computer to run applications and games – not for running an OS – didn't you?

items.title: Intel reportedly preparing Razor Lake-S CPU with 12 P-cores and 120MB of cache
items.summary: Intel's 12 P-core Razor Lake-S compute die reportedly measures around 140 mm² Nearly two weeks ago, we reported that Intel was preparing a dedicated 12 P-core compute die for its...
body: Nearly two weeks ago, we reported that Intel was preparing a dedicated 12 P-core compute die for its Razor Lake-S desktop processor series. Hardware leaker Jaykihn has now shared more information about this silicon, including its cache capacity and estimated die size.

According to the leaker, the 12+0 compute die will feature 120MB of Big Last Level Cache (bLLC). The processor will have no standard E-cores but will still feature four low-power E-cores, bringing the total CPU core count to 16. Intel reportedly plans to manufacture this compute die using its own 18A-P process.
The 12 P-Core variant is something Intel never launched for gamers, although we did get a bit of taste of such a config with Bartlett Lake-S, except it was never a gaming CPU to begin with.

Jaykihn estimates that the die measures around 140 mm², although he has yet to verify this figure. Unlike other Razor Lake-S compute tiles, this design will reportedly retain the Coyote Cove P-core architecture from Nova Lake rather than adopt Griffin Cove.

The leaker also claims that the 8+16 Razor Lake-S compute tile will feature 144MB of bLLC, matching the cache capacity of the equivalent Nova Lake-S design. This means the dedicated 12 P-core die will have four more P-cores but 24MB less L3 cache.

items.title: Makita power tool battery pack adapter tested as portable laptop power solution
items.summary: Leading power tool firm Makita has released an adapter for its battery packs, allowing them to be used for charging phones, tablets, and even laptops. A Japanese PC magazine has tested its laptop companion prowess.
body: Alternative laptop power solution could appeal to road warriors who have a collection of drill batteries.

PC Watch contributor Masahiro Yamaguchi already had a Makita power tool with a BL1830B 3,000mAh capacity 18V battery pack, so this was used in testing. Yamaguchi noted that Makita sells and bundles compatible power packs with as much as 12,000mAh capacity, and the more spare Makita power tool batteries you have in your house/garage, the more attractive the ADP15 adapter becomes.

Before checking the Type-C PD100 port's laptop charging capabilities, the ADP15 was assessed with the USB Cable Checker3 gadget. It was found to support both Programmable Power Supply (PPS), which is part of the USB Power Delivery 3.0 specification, and Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS). Yamaguchi thought that this spec level made the ADP15 "quite feature rich" [machine translation].

An iPhone 17 Pro Max was connected next, and it seemed to charge near its maximum limit, at 37W. Then, at last, the ADP15's USB PD port was hooked up to a Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 9. It was observed that the laptop charged at about 60W, though the PC is supposed to support 65W charging. That's pretty close, though. Yamaguchi's 3,000mAh battery managed to charge the Lenovo up to about 77% full. On that point, readers were reminded that there are Makita battery packs with up to 12,000mAh capacity, and many keen DIYers will have several packs.

items.title: Hair dye that turns your head into a brain-computer interface
items.summary: eHAIR is claimed to transform hair 'from a barrier into a functional bioelectronic interface.'
body: Tech could narrow the gap between non-invasive brain computer interfaces and implanted solutions like Neuralink.

eHAIR is claimed to transform hair "from a barrier into a functional bioelectronic interface." One approach that was tested uses highly conductive, low-impedance coatings that are readily applied and removed. Another bottom-up strategy grows conductive polymers directly on single hair strands. These complementary approaches yield stable, low-impedance, and highly conductive interfaces "that enable gel-free, comfortable EEG acquisition and direct compatibility with conventional hardware and human hair and skin," assert the researchers.

The nature of eHAIR creates potential applications beyond passive electrodes. Researchers highlighted that organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) can be formed using individual hairs or hair bundles. So, the hair(s) can also act as transistor channels and could be used to amplify signals, for example.

Testing has shown that eHAIR facilitates improved signal amplitude, spectral power, and SNR compared to conventional gel-based electrodes. Medical professionals just have to reapply the coating or repeat the polymerization process if hair grows and degrades the electrical contact. This task isn't very complicated, with the scientists likening it to routine household hair coloring techniques.

body: Bilibili creator 51972 traced recurring game stutter on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D system to an interaction between GIGABYTE Control Center and an NVIDIA driver. The investigation began with a viewer who suspected the Ryzen processor was causing stutter across multiple games. The 51972 team reproduced the issue on matching hardware using a clone of the viewer’s drive. The team found that the frame-time spikes followed the rhythm of the graphics card’s RGB animation.

bilibili 51972 analyzed another "amdip" case. after a month of investigation, he eventually found that the stuttering had nothing to do with the 9800x3d. instead, it was caused by a combination of a new nvidia driver, gigabyte gcc software, and a gigabyte gpu that supports not… https://t.co/ietpJKKlH9 pic.twitter.com/ip9qPWRkXh

As AI servers like Rubin Ultra push PCB layers toward 78 layers using denser laminates, drill bits are wearing out 10 times faster than normal, while high-speed signalling stretches the demand for smooth copper foil.
body: More than 20 Chinese PCB manufacturers announced major expansion plans in the first half of 2026. Three recent reports from HSBC and J.P. Morgan suggest the shortages could extend to products as unglamorous as drill bits and copper foil. Having a plentiful and regular supply of those components in the manufacturing process is important because the tiny drill bit used to make the circuit boards inside AI servers could be worn out after drilling fewer than 200 holes, according to HSBC, compared with around 2,000 holes for older materials.
It’s all part of a manufacturing process which stresses every part of the supply and manufacturing chain, beyond obvious components.

PCBs are built by layering copper and insulating material together, then drilling holes through them to connect their circuits. But the complexity of those boards is increasing as AI servers are designed to handle more data, including more layers than those seen in ordinary computers. HSBC estimates that a notebook PCB has four to eight layers, compared with more than 20 for Nvidia's H100 generation of GPUs.
But that’s just the beginning of the process.

body: NVIDIA has agreed to pay $290 million to settle a US shareholder lawsuit over how it reported the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GeForce sales. The parties filed the agreement on November 24, 2026. The settlement still requires court approval.

The lawsuit began in December 2018 and covers eligible investors who acquired NVIDIA common stock between August 10, 2017 and November 15, 2018. NVIDIA and CEO Jensen Huang deny the allegations. The agreement includes no admission of wrongdoing.

The case centers on the GeForce GTX 10 series. Investors alleged that miners bought GeForce cards and that NVIDIA counted those sales as gaming revenue. They said NVIDIA and Huang gave investors the impression that most crypto-related sales came from dedicated mining products reported under its OEM business.

In November 2018, NVIDIA lowered its revenue outlook and said excess GPU inventory was weighing on its results after the crypto boom. NVIDIA shares fell 28.5% over the next two trading sessions, according to the plaintiffs’ filing.

A federal court dismissed the case in 2021, but the Ninth Circuit revived part of it in 2023. The US Supreme Court dropped its review in December 2024, leaving the appeals court ruling in place. The motion for preliminary approval lists February 4, 2027 as the hearing date.

body: The number of Xbox Series emulation projects continues to grow following the leak of the GTA VI Xbox build. Developer Zortos has announced XSEmu, a project that combines its own Xbox compatibility layer with several third-party emulator forks under a single graphical interface.

XSEmu is based on the XCL translation layer. It executes Xbox Series game code directly on x86-64 processors rather than emulating the console hardware. The software translates Xbox-specific Direct3D 12.X calls into standard Direct3D 12 calls and recompiles RDNA2 shaders for PC graphics cards.

According to the developer, the XSEmu core is currently optimized for NVIDIA graphics cards in the GeForce RTX 3080 performance class and below. AMD Radeon users will have access to alternative emulator forks through the same launcher. Native AMD support for the XSEmu core is planned for later.

The launcher allows users to select Xbox Series S or Series X mode and assign a different runner to each game. It also features shader pipeline precompilation with pause and resume functionality. Compilation automatically pauses when available system memory drops below 1GB.

body: Another GeForce RTX 5070 owner has reported a melted power connector, but this time the damage occurred on the power supply side. Reddit user lil_zoghi shared a photo of a damaged 8-pin modular connector on an ASUS ROG Strix 650W power supply. The graphics card itself remains functional, according to the owner.

The system uses an MSI GeForce RTX 5070 SHADOW 2X with a 16-pin power adapter. The owner claims the graphics card was undervolted and consumed no more than 180W, compared to its default 250W power rating.

What makes this case interesting is that this is reportedly the second power supply to suffer such damage in the same user’s system. The owner had previously used the ASUS power supply with a GeForce RTX 3070 without encountering similar problems.

The owner later confirmed that only one modular PCIe connection on the power supply was used to feed the 16-pin adapter. NVIDIA recommends using two separate PCIe 8-pin cables with the RTX 5070 adapter. The user acknowledged overlooking the instructions included with the graphics card.

items.title: TSMC gives a sneap peak at AI Design Kit: Agentic AI with foundry expertise
items.summary: TSMC brings agentic AI to chip design as A14 design rule count hits 3.6X that of N5 while customers demand 33% shorter development cycle.
body: TSMC's ADK promises to cut accelerate chip development as nodes get more complex.

At its 2026 Europe OIP Ecosystem Workshop in Munich, TSMC this week unveiled its AI Design Kit (ADK), a collection of process-specific technical information, implementation guidelines, and design methodologies that enables AI agents to automate and optimize chip development flows.

The ADK complements the foundry's traditional process design kits (PDKs) and enables AI agents to use TSMC's process-specific expertise, knowledge of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, and customers' proprietary design methodologies to automate physical implementation and optimization of chips. Ultimately, the initiative aims to reduce development cycles, improve design productivity, and simplify adoption of TSMC's advanced process technologies.

"The ADK complements our traditional PDK, and it brings in capabilities to augment the EDA and other design flows," said Aveek Sarkar, Head of Ecosystem and Alliance Management at TSMC. "Our goal with these agentic flows is to bring in the technology-specific learning we have at TSMC and layer that with your orchestration layer, with your design expertise, and to support the next generation of EDA or design flows and methodologies that you have."

items.title: Intel Moon Lake reportedly features a 19% smaller compute die than Wildcat Lake
items.summary: Intel Wildcat Lake Refresh reportedly uses 18A-P with 21% larger compute die, Moon Lake is 19% smaller Intel's three budget mobile architectures will share the same platform controller die. Intel...
body: Intel’s three budget mobile architectures will share the same platform controller die.

Intel is reportedly preparing two new processor designs for entry-level laptops based on the Wildcat Lake platform. Hardware leaker Jaykihn has now shared compute die sizes and manufacturing nodes for Wildcat Lake, Wildcat Lake Refresh and Moon Lake.

The information reveals that Wildcat Lake Refresh will use Intel 18A-P, an enhanced version of the manufacturing process used for the current Wildcat Lake series. The compute die will measure 93.30 mm², up from 77.42 mm², representing a 20.5% increase in silicon area.

As we reported in June, Wildcat Lake Refresh will feature up to four Cougar Cove P-cores and four Darkmont LP-E cores. Jaykihn confirmed that the additional 15.88 mm² accommodates two extra Performance cores and 6MB of L3 cache. According to the leaker, Intel is developing the refreshed design because the current Wildcat Lake series is not competitive enough against Apple’s MacBook Neo.

Moon Lake uses a smaller 62.79 mm² compute dieMoon Lake goes in the opposite direction. The processor reportedly removes both Performance cores and retains four Darkmont LP-E cores. Its Intel 18A compute die measures 62.79 mm², making it 18.9% smaller than Wildcat Lake. As we reported last month, Moon Lake is designed for a default power configuration of 6W.

items.title: Kioxia's 3rd-gen XL-Flash hits Optane-class 3-microsecond read latency with 70% higher density
items.summary: Kioxia showed an XL-Flash Generation 3 prototype at KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo and named the upcoming GP2 SSD as its first product.
body: Its first home is the GP2 SSD, rated for more than 18 million random reads per second.

The low-latency XL-Flash fills “a new memory tier” to bridge the gap between DRAM and regular flash memory, in a way that can complement or replace some DRAM to help drive down costs, especially in AI servers and data centers. This has some similarities to Optane, which used 3D XPoint instead, as a storage class memory (SCM) option to reach higher IOPS. Intel and Micron’s 3D XPoint stored bits as changes in the cell material’s resistance rather than as trapped charge like NAND, and Intel exited the Optane business in 2022. The XL-Flash NAND is built on BiCS flash technology, but it’s tuned for low read latency and high write endurance.

The first generation was SLC with under-5 µs reads, arriving in 2019. By 2022, Gen 2 added 2-bit MLC as an option for lower bit cost, trading some like-for-like performance for better price-to-density. Gen 3 is reported to use SLC, and its 3 µs average read latency challenges the first gen’s sub-5 µs rating while being more than ten times faster than the 40 µs of standard BiCS8 TLC. This is within the same ballpark as Optane SSDs. The flash also reportedly has SLC endurance at 150,000 to 250,000 P/E cycles, at least 50x standard TLC, running at a 4.8 Gb/s interface speed.

items.title: GTA VI comes full circle, now running on PS5-based crypto mining hardware
items.summary: From console gaming to crypto mining and back to gaming There is some irony in the latest development surrounding the unofficial PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI. The leaked...
body: There is some irony in the latest development surrounding the unofficial PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI. The leaked PlayStation 5 version of the game is now reportedly running on AMD BC-250 hardware, a cryptocurrency mining board based on the very same silicon developed for Sony’s console.

As some of our readers may remember, we first covered the BC-250 in 2022. AMD repurposed PS5 silicon for cryptocurrency mining systems manufactured by ASRock. The board features six Zen 2 CPU cores, 24 RDNA 2 Compute Units and 16GB of GDDR6 memory.

Following the decline of GPU cryptocurrency mining, these boards found their way into the hands of PC enthusiasts. Community-developed drivers and modifications have since turned the BC-250 into an inexpensive Linux gaming system. We previously covered such hardware running GTA V and Cyberpunk 2077.

Now, developer djaye has demonstrated GTA VI running on the BC-250. Interestingly, the developer clarified that this is not based on the Kyty project. The exact method and performance characteristics have yet to be detailed.

So here we are. Silicon originally designed to run PlayStation 5 games, repurposed by AMD for cryptocurrency mining and later converted into a PC by enthusiasts, is now running a PlayStation 5 game that has yet to receive an official PC release.

items.title: Intel Razor Lake-AX reportedly features two variants: 96GB MoP and 192GB MoB
items.summary: Intel Razor Lake-AX to feature two memory configurations Intel is reportedly developing two separate product lines based on its Razor Lake-AX processor. According to hardware leaker Jaykihn, Intel plans to...
body: Intel is reportedly developing two separate product lines based on its Razor Lake-AX processor. According to hardware leaker Jaykihn, Intel plans to offer variants with Memory-on-Package (MoP) and Memory-on-Motherboard (MoB). The latter is said to support up to 192GB of memory.

Yesterday, we reported on a leaked Razor Lake-AX prototype featuring four memory chips installed directly on the processor package. According to our information, Intel intends to let OEM and ODM partners install the memory themselves. Jaykihn claims that the MoP product line officially supports up to 96GB, although I will mention that I heard about 128GB config as well.

Jaykihn also shared two silicon configurations for Razor Lake-AX. The smaller variant features 4 P-cores, 8 E-cores, 4 low-power E-cores and 16 Xe3 graphics cores. The larger variant features 8 P-cores, 16 E-cores, 4 low-power E-cores and 32 Xe3 graphics cores.

128GB/256GB respectively between MoP/MoB are unofficially supported, but Intel believes the allocation required is practically impossible for the OEM. There are no projected suppliers available for the required 32GB package.

The distinction between these configurations is separate from the two memory product lines. However, Intel currently plans to use only the larger 28-core configuration for the MoB series. According to the leaker, this product line is still being defined.

items.title: AMD RDNA 5 graphics support is coming to Linux 7.5
items.summary: AMD prepares Linux kernel support for its next-generation Radeon GPUs AMD has submitted another round of AMDGPU driver updates targeting the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel. The November 26 pull request...
body: AMD has submitted another round of AMDGPU driver updates targeting the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel. The November 26 pull request for DRM-Next includes early support for Graphics Core 13 (GC13), the graphics architecture expected to power AMD’s RDNA 5 GPUs.

As we reported earlier this month, AMD had already published eight patches adding more than 12,600 lines of driver code for GFX13. Those patches covered two graphics IP versions, GFX 13.0.1 and GFX 13.0.4. The latest submission puts this work on track for inclusion in Linux 7.5.
The pull request includes support and updates for several hardware blocks associated with AMD’s next-generation graphics architecture:

AMD has also started preparing GFX13 support for the RadeonSI OpenGL and RADV Vulkan drivers in Mesa. Both kernel and userspace driver development are now underway for the upcoming graphics architecture.

Linux 7.5 is expected to reach stable release in the first quarter of 2027. The GFX13 support is still experimental and more driver updates will be required before the hardware becomes commercially available.
AMD has yet to announce its next-generation Radeon graphics cards. According to previous leaks, the first RDNA 5 products could arrive in the second half of 2027, with more models following in 2028.

Meanwhile Rockstar Games is silent on PC version and mulitplayer plansWhat makes this development unusual is that Rockstar has yet to launch its own multiplayer mode, let alone announce a release date for the PC version. items.title: G.Skill says this PCB corner mark is enough to void your lifetime RAM warranty
items.summary: G.Skill customer denied lifetime warranty over scratch A Redditor has shared their experience with G.Skill's limited lifetime memory warranty. The company reportedly rejected an RMA request for a Ripjaws V...
body: A Redditor has shared their experience with G.Skill’s limited lifetime memory warranty. The company reportedly rejected an RMA request for a Ripjaws V DDR4-3200 16GB (2x8GB) memory kit manufactured in May 2023, citing physical damage to the PCB.

According to the customer, the memory passes memory tests but causes system crashes after three to four hours of gaming. G.Skill provided a close-up photo showing damage to the outer corner of the PCB as justification for rejecting the warranty claim. The customer requested another evaluation, but the RMA department upheld its decision after consulting a manager.

To be fair, this is still physical damage, so G.Skill has grounds to dispute the warranty claim. However, the damage appears to be limited to the outer edge of the PCB, away from any visible traces, contacts or components. We doubt that this mark alone would cause memory instability, although a photo cannot rule out internal PCB damage.
We also asked an expert and repair technican VIK-on. Basically said that perhaps the user is not telling the full story.
The situation is more complex than it might seem at first glance.

items.title: DXVK 3.2 brings smoother frame pacing to Linux gaming
items.summary: DXVK 3.2 adds Vulkan present timing support for smoother gaming on Wayland DXVK 3.2 has been released with support for the VK_EXT_present_timing Vulkan extension. The feature allows DXVK to achieve...
body: DXVK 3.2 has been released with support for the VK_EXT_present_timing Vulkan extension. The feature allows DXVK to achieve more consistent frame pacing when using its built-in FPS limiter or running games at non-native refresh rates in fullscreen mode. The latter is important on Wayland, where DXVK cannot directly change the display mode and must emulate lower refresh rates.

The feature requires vertical synchronization and a compatible graphics driver and compositor. It works with recent Gamescope builds or Wayland-enabled Proton builds such as Proton-GE when used with a compositor supporting the commit-timing-v1 protocol. The developer notes that manually setting DXVK’s FPS limiter may also improve frame pacing in games that already have their own 60 FPS limit.

DXVK 3.2 improves its VRAM eviction logic, which should benefit games running on graphics cards with limited video memory. The update also changes how Direct3D 11 resources are uploaded to reduce stuttering. Shader code generation has been improved in several cases.

Interestingly, GitHub used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI to highlight the project’s popularity, despite actively processing copyright takedown requests targeting unofficial PC ports of the same game.

The official GitHub account on X celebrated AnyPS5 reaching 58,000 stars since its August launch. The accompanying video also highlighted developers working on the translation layer ahead of the GTA VI release. GitHub even asked its followers whether changing the platform on which games run crosses a legal line.

As we reported two months ago, AnyPS5 takes a different approach from traditional console emulators. It converts PS5 executables into native Windows and Linux programs and replaces the console’s system libraries with its own implementations. The project has now reached 61,900 stars, 6,000 forks and over 51,000 commits. However, AnyPS5 has yet to demonstrate GTA VI running on PC.

Just two days ago, GitHub processed a DMCA notice from Take-Two covering the entire Leonida repository network. As we reported yesterday, this resulted in the removal of 3,007 repositories associated with an unofficial PC port based on the Xbox version of GTA VI.

items.title: Thermal Grizzly launches first CPU delidding accessory with Intel Nova Lake support
items.summary: Delid-Heat-Mate already supports LGA-1954 processors Thermal Grizzly has launched its Delid-Heat-Mate, a new accessory designed to assist in removing integrated heat spreaders (IHS) from processors. What makes this release interesting...
body: Thermal Grizzly has launched its Delid-Heat-Mate, a new accessory designed to assist in removing integrated heat spreaders (IHS) from processors. What makes this release interesting is that Thermal Grizzly already lists support for Intel’s upcoming LGA-1954 socket, which will be used by Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs.

This is not the first Thermal Grizzly product to support the upcoming Intel platform. Back in September, we covered the launch of the Mycro Pro Stainless Steel CPU water blocks with LGA-1954 support. However, this appears to be the first commercially available delidding accessory to explicitly support Nova Lake.

Interestingly, Thermal Grizzly confirms that Nova Lake CPUs will require the same two-stage delidding process as Arrow Lake. While heating is optional for AMD AM5 and Intel LGA-1700 processors, the company states that it is necessary for both LGA-1851 and LGA-1954 CPUs.

The Delid-Heat-Mate works in combination with a separately sold Delid-Die-Mate tool. Once the adhesive and solder bonds have been mechanically loosened, the processor is placed upside down in the new accessory and heated in an oven at 165-175°C. The indium solder melts at approximately 157°C, allowing the heat spreader to detach under its own weight. The process typically takes 10 to 15 minutes.

items.summary: Apple reportedly preparing two MacBook Air updates Apple may launch its first MacBook Air with an OLED display as early as next year. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman revealed in the latest...
body: Apple may launch its first MacBook Air with an OLED display as early as next year. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman revealed in the latest episode of his Power On podcast that Apple is preparing a major redesign of its thin-and-light laptop for late 2027 or 2028.

Before that happens, Apple plans to refresh its MacBook Air lineup with the M6 processor in spring 2027. The new 13-inch and 15-inch models, internally known as J913 and J915, respectively, will reportedly launch alongside the second-generation MacBook Neo. Gurman does not expect major design changes for this generation.

Apple introduced the current MacBook Air design in 2022 with the M2 processor, replacing the wedge-shaped chassis with a uniform thickness design. The company expanded the series with a 15-inch model in 2023.

Gurman previously suggested that Apple would introduce OLED displays to the MacBook Air series in 2028 at the earliest. Last month, the reporter confirmed that Apple was internally testing OLED-equipped MacBook Air and iMac models. The latest information suggests the MacBook Air redesign could arrive earlier.

Launching two MacBook Air generations in one year would be unusual, but Apple did precisely that with its MacBook Pro series in 2026. The company released its M5 Pro and M5 Max refresh in March before introducing redesigned models with PROLED XDR displays in October.

items.title: Free OLED Engine Windows app offers burn-in protection for up to five monitors
items.summary: OLED protection without manufacturer-specific software A Redditor has released OLED Engine, a free Windows application designed to reduce the risk of OLED burn-in. The software also works with non-OLED displays...
body: A Redditor has released OLED Engine, a free Windows application designed to reduce the risk of OLED burn-in. The software also works with non-OLED displays and supports up to five monitors, each with independently configurable protection settings.

OLED Engine can automatically dim or switch idle displays to pure black, effectively turning off individual pixels on OLED panels. The software can also hide desktop icons, the Windows taskbar and the mouse cursor. Users can configure automatic display shutdown, track screen usage and receive pixel refresh reminders.

We previously covered Monarch, another community-developed Windows application that allows users to disable individual monitors through keyboard shortcuts. OLED Engine expands on a similar concept with automated display management based on user activity.

The application supports different idle timers for desktop use, gaming, competitive gaming and paused video playback. It can detect video playback and controller input to avoid unwanted dimming. Users can also configure individual application profiles, brightness levels, dimming speeds and keyboard shortcuts.

OLED Engine supports automatic HDR and SDR switching, including an option to disable HDR when launching competitive games. GeForce owners can also configure automatic G-SYNC switching through NVIDIA Profile Inspector, although this feature requires administrator privileges and additional configuration.

items.title: No Man’s Sky finally gets AMD FSR 4 support thanks to Vulkan SDK update
items.summary: Another Vulkan game gets AMD machine learning upscaling Hello Games has released update 7.15 for No Man's Sky, adding support for AMD FSR 4 upscaling. The game is among the...
body: Hello Games has released update 7.15 for No Man’s Sky, adding support for AMD FSR 4 upscaling. The game is among the first Vulkan titles to receive native support for AMD’s machine learning-based upscaling technology.

Back in September, No Man’s Sky engine programmer Martin Griffiths explained why the game did not support FSR 4. The PC version uses a Vulkan renderer, while AMD’s technology was restricted to DirectX 12 at the time. Griffiths publicly expressed interest in bringing FSR 4 to the game once AMD added Vulkan support.
AMD recently added Vulkan support to their FSR SDK 2.4, allowing us to bring FSR 4 to #NoMansSky. It’s available today as part of our 7.15 update! https://t.co/bnFqnYhin4

AMD addressed this limitation with the release of FSR Redstone SDK 2.4 on October 28. The SDK introduced Vulkan support alongside FSR Upscaling 4.1.2, extending machine learning-based upscaling to Radeon RX 6000 graphics cards and select Ryzen APUs.

As we reported last week, DOOM: The Dark Ages became the first Vulkan game to support both FSR Upscaling 4.1 and Frame Generation 4. No Man’s Sky now follows with its own upscaling implementation, although Hello Games has not announced support for AMD’s latest frame generation technology.

body: The unofficial GTA 6 PC projects are now targeting graphics cards without hardware ray tracing support. A video shared on Reddit reportedly shows the game running on a Radeon RX 580, a graphics card that AMD released in April 2017.

The 22-second video shows what can best be described as a slideshow rather than gameplay. The Redditor who shared the footage admitted that they did not even expect the game to get past the loading screens.

Another developer has reportedly managed to run GTA 6 on the same GPU using a custom branch of the VIctory project with a compute-based fallback for mesh shaders. The developer is using a Core i5-9600K processor, 32GB of RAM and a Radeon RX 580 8GB running Windows 10. The game runs in Xbox Series S mode at low settings with performance of around 1 FPS.
The developer plans to release a package targeting the Radeon RX 580 and older graphics cards once the software is stable. There is no release date yet, and the project is not publicly available.

As we reported yesterday, several groups are working on unofficial GTA 6 PC builds despite Take-Two’s efforts to remove related repositories. While the latest footage is far from playable and has yet to be independently verified, it suggests that developers are already experimenting with hardware that predates both current-generation consoles and consumer GPUs with hardware ray tracing.

items.title: Intel Razor Lake-AX prototype leaks out, features four on-package memory modules
items.summary: Intel Razor Lake-AX to support up to 128GB of on-package memory An alleged Intel Razor Lake-AX prototype has surfaced online. Someone appears to be selling a used processor sample that...
body: An alleged Intel Razor Lake-AX prototype has surfaced online. Someone appears to be selling a used processor sample that is either damaged or was discarded during development. It is unclear whether the processor is still functional. However, the photograph appears to confirm one of the rumored features of Razor Lake-AX: on-package memory.

The processor features four memory ICs installed directly on the same package as the CPU. In this regard, Razor Lake-AX is expected to compete with AMD’s Halo series of processors, which are predominantly used in systems equipped with LPDDR5X memory.

According to our information, Razor Lake-AX currently supports memory configurations ranging from 32GB to 128GB. What makes Intel’s approach different is that the company plans to supply the processor to OEM and ODM partners without memory installed. Partners will be responsible for installing the four DRAM ICs during manufacturing.

We have also learned that Razor Lake-AX is expected to feature up to 32 GPU cores and a quad-channel memory interface. Intel is reportedly targeting the third quarter of 2027 for the first Razor Lake-AX products, although this schedule is subject to change.

items.title: ASUS ROG XG Station 3 Thunderbolt 5 eGPU dock officially costs €399
items.summary: ASUS ROG XG Station 3 goes on sale 18 months after its debut ASUS has officially launched its ROG XG Station 3 external graphics card dock in Europe. The company...
body: ASUS has officially launched its ROG XG Station 3 external graphics card dock in Europe. The company has confirmed a recommended retail price of €399 including VAT in Germany and Austria, with Swiss pricing set at CHF 399. This price does not include a graphics card or a power supply.

We first covered the XG Station 3 at Computex 2025 in May last year. ASUS took nearly 18 months to bring the product to market. The company announced the final product earlier this month but did not confirm pricing at the time.

The XG Station 3 features an open design with support for desktop graphics cards up to 360 mm long and 93 mm thick. One of its main features is the GC-HPWR connector, which allows compatible ASUS BTF graphics cards such as the ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 BTF Edition to operate without an external GPU power cable.

The dock uses a Thunderbolt 5 interface with up to 80 Gbps of bidirectional bandwidth and up to 140W of laptop charging. It also features a secondary Thunderbolt 5 port with 36W power delivery and support for up to three 4K displays. ASUS has included two additional 10 Gbps USB Type-C ports.
